title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 106
paragraphs: When the king, being at that time in Sardis, was setting the Persian army in motion to march against Athens, Hermotimos, having gone down on some business to that part of Mysia occupied by the Chians and called Atarneus, found Panionios there. Recognizing him, he spoke to him with many friendly words — first recounting all the good things he now had through him, and next making promises in return, saying how many benefits he would do for him if he would bring his household and settle in that land; so that Panionios gladly accepting the offer, brought his children and his wife. Then, when Hermotimos had him in his grasp together with his whole household, he spoke as follows: “You — who of all men who ever lived until now, gained your substance by the most impious deeds — what evil did I myself or any of my forefathers ever do to you or yours, that you made me a nothing instead of a man? Did you suppose you would escape the notice of the gods for the things you devised? They, following the rule of justice, delivered you into my hands for your impious deeds, so that you shall have no cause to complain of the penalty I shall inflict upon you.” Having reproached him thus, he had the man's sons brought into his presence, and Panionios was compelled to castrate his own sons, four in number; and once compelled, he did so. Then, when he had done this, the sons were compelled to do the same thing to him. Thus did vengeance at the hands of Hermotimos overtake Panionios.
